A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PP/OK-type neuropeptides have a myorelaxing function in starfish, whereas they are myoexciting in protostomians.
the neuropeptides of starfish are similar to the neuropeptides in other echinoderms and that they are also related to the neuropeptidergic signaling in protostomia.
the PP/OK type neuromuscular transmitter system in starfish is more similar to that in vertebrates than to that in protostomians.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neuropeptide SMP (ArPplN1b) causes dose dependent relaxation (myorelaxant effect) of starfish muscle in vitro.
the neuropeptide ArPPLN1 is a muscle relaxant that acts in a deuteromian invertebrate, starfish, to inhibit muscle contraction.
neuropeptides can have opposite functions in different animal phyla.
